inputConstruction.claim: The complete ClassifierBatch each logical batch sends is constructed deterministically from the committed DEVELOPMENT canonical corpus rows plus three production version constants. This is a reconstruction defined by this freeze; it does not claim to reproduce the lost 2D2B runner’s unknown batch bytes.

documents.source: the exact canonical `document` object of every corpus row belonging to the organisation
documents.docIndex: each document keeps its original docIndex; nothing is renumbered

context.organisationName: the exact common organisationName of the organisation’s corpus rows
context.echeRowKey: the exact common echeRowKey of the organisation’s corpus rows
context.countryCode: the exact common countryCode of the organisation’s corpus rows
context.runId: the exact common runId of the organisation’s corpus rows
context.roots: the union of every document.roots entry in the organisation batch, deduplicated by exact rootKey, sorted by rootKey using ordinal string comparison (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0)

preconditions: every corpus row of an organisation agrees exactly on organisationName, echeRowKey, countryCode and runId; on any disagreement construction stops
a rootKey that appears on more than one document carries byte-identical authorityKind and url on every occurrence; on any disagreement construction stops and no version is chosen
the batch-level roots union includes only roots represented by the selected canonical DEVELOPMENT documents; no database, mixed corpus or HOLDOUT file is read to recover further run roots
inputConstruction.serialization: canonicalStringify({ context, documents }) as implemented in src/orgunits/classify/canonical.ts (sorted object keys, arrays in given order), encoded as UTF-8
inputConstruction.assemblyInputSha256: lowercase hex SHA-256 of exactly those UTF-8 bytes
inputConstruction.canonicalSerializedInputSha256: equal to assemblyInputSha256 by definition; both names are retained only because the output-capture contract already used the former
inputConstruction.finalInputSha256: computeFinalInputSha256({ assemblyInputSha256, promptVersion, outputSchemaVersion: "orgunit-classifier-output-schema-v2" }) as implemented in src/orgunits/classify/finalIdentity.ts
invariants: exactly 12 assembly identities, one per logical batch, byte-identical to F0B’s (the inputs are the same bytes attempt 1 read)
exactly 12 final identities, one per logical batch, each computeFinalInputSha256({ assemblyInputSha256, promptVersion: orgunit-classifier-prompt-v3, outputSchemaVersion })
the V3 final identity of every batch differs from both attempt-1 final identities of that batch, which are carried as attempt1ComparatorFinalInputSha256 for pairing provenance only
no two batches share an assembly identity; no two batches share a V3 final identity
recomputation from the committed corpus produces the same values on every run

the repair policy enters NO identity: a repair call’s own input_sha256 is derived by computeRepairInputSha256 over the original identity plus the repair request bytes (ADR 0011), and the final input identity of an evaluation is unchanged whether the policy is enabled or disabled
the 13 historical assemblyInputSha256 values on the corpus rows are never reused as an identity

claudeCodeExecutable.contract: The provider resolves the exact native binary bundled by the exact installed SDK from the variant root’s own node_modules ONCE per classify(), fails closed on a missing optional native package, a path outside node_modules, a symlink or non-regular file, any version disagreement, a non-executable binary, a byte-length or SHA-256 mismatch against the SDK’s own manifest, an unsupported platform or an ambiguous resolution, and hands that one path to BOTH the request-free auth-status preflight and the Agent SDK invocation (pathToClaudeCodeExecutable). The production builder and the F1 POSIX child allowlist forward USER by name; no artifact, test or report records its value. The root cause inside Claude Code is not known and is not claimed.

classifier.inputIdentity: input_sha256 = computeFinalInputSha256(assemblyInputSha256, promptVersion, outputSchemaVersion) as implemented at the variant commit. The V3 identity of every batch differs from both attempt-1 identities of that batch by construction (the prompt version differs), so no attempt-1 result can be reused for a V3 question and no V3 result can shadow one. The exact values are frozen per batch in batching.plan.finalInputSha256.PROMPT_V3_CANONICAL and are recomputed by the F0E unit test (exactly as the F0C unit test recomputed them; the prompt version, and therefore every identity, is unchanged by the runtime re-pin). A repair call carries its own derived input_sha256 (computeRepairInputSha256) and is never a plan identity.

repairDeadlineFormula.statement: repairWindowMs = max(0, remainingLogicalEvaluationBudgetMsAtRepairDecision - CLASSIFIER_CALL_HARD_KILL_GRACE_MS); for EVERY adapter/runner attempt of the repair: repairAttemptDeadlineMs = min(CLASSIFIER_CALL_SOFT_DEADLINE_MS, max(0, repairWindowMs - elapsedSinceRepairClassifyEntryMs)), where elapsedSinceRepairClassifyEntryMs includes all time already spent inside that repair call (pre-flight and auth-status, prior transient attempts, retry backoff). A non-positive remainder is the existing terminal TIMEOUT with no new runner attempt. The minimum-remaining-budget gate (repairWindowMs < REPAIR_MINIMUM_REMAINING_BUDGET_MS -> skip, fail closed) is applied BEFORE any repair request is opened.
implementation: orchestrator / child: elapsedMs = clock.now() - originalEnteredAt, measured immediately before each repair decision; remainingMs = max(0, 600000 - elapsedMs); usableMs = max(0, remainingMs - 10000)
gate: if usableMs < minimumRemainingBudgetMs -> REPAIR_SKIPPED_INSUFFICIENT_BUDGET, persisted, zero provider calls (strict less-than; applied before the repair call row and before classify())
window: the provider receives totalBudgetMs = usableMs and opens it at classify() ENTRY, so pre-flight and the auth-status check spend it; it is never widened beyond 600000

per attempt: deadlineMs = min(300000, totalBudgetMs - elapsedSinceEntry); a non-positive remainder is a terminal TIMEOUT with zero runner calls; transient retries and their backoff stay inside the same window

grace: the 10000 ms hard-kill grace is reserved by subtracting it from remainingMs before the window is handed over; the runner spends it only after a deadline expires, so a repair ends no later than originalEnteredAt + 600000 ms

consequence: the FIRST attempt receives min(300000, repairWindowMs - preflightAndAuthStatusMs); every LATER attempt additionally loses the earlier attempts and their backoff; no attempt ever receives more than the frozen 300000 ms soft deadline nor more than remaining - 10000
provedBy: src/test/unit/orgunitClassifyRepair.test.ts (decideRepairBudget: window and first-attempt deadline arithmetic, boundaries, non-positive guard)

src/test/unit/orgunitClassifyClaudeMaxProvider.test.ts (the caller window through the real adapter: never wider than the frozen total, opened at entry, spent by auth status; a repair attempt never exceeds 300000 ms; the general rule for a LATER attempt - auth status, an earlier attempt and its backoff all reduce the next deadline - and the exhausted case with no further runner attempt)
src/test/integration/orgunitClassifyRepairOrchestrate.test.ts (the orchestrator hands the provider exactly remaining - grace)

minimumRemainingBudgetMsOptions.note: The floor compares usableMs = remainingMs - 10000 (the grace is already outside it) with a strict less-than. Two options were presented; the owner SELECTED 120000 ms on the usable window on 2026-09-14 and REJECTED 60000 ms. The implementation constant and this file now carry 120000. The selection is a readiness threshold, not a proof that a repair succeeds, and it is NOT a freeze approval.

measuredOnAttempt1.slowestFullEvaluationRef: PROMPT_V1_CANONICAL batch-10 provider-outcome.json monotonicWallTimeMs (includes its own auth-status check; one adapter attempt)

options.semantics: Guarantees only that a repair request is OPENED. If the auth-status check takes its full 60000 ms upper bound, the repair times out before any runner attempt (a persisted FAILED / TIMEOUT repair row, zero inference); if it exceeds it, AUTH_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE. Typical auth-status time is far below the bound (attempt-1 whole evaluations took 10-50 s including it), but that is an observation, not a guarantee.

After a worst-case 60000 ms auth-status check, at least 60000 ms of inference window remains, which exceeds the slowest observed attempt-1 FULL evaluation (50179 ms, itself including auth status) by 9821 ms; a single-document repair is smaller than any full batch. The hard-kill grace is reserved separately by the orchestrator, so the owner-suggested decomposition 60000 + 50000 + 10000 double-counts the grace when read against usableMs; read against remainingMs it is 130000, which this option provides.
options.mechanicalDerivation: usableFloorMs >= AUTH_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS (60000) + slowestObservedFullEvaluationWallMs (50179) = 110179 ms; 120000 is the smallest round figure at or above it, leaving 9821 ms headroom.

minimumRemainingBudgetMsOptions.recommendation: usableFloorMs = 120000 (remainingFloorMs = 130000), SELECTED by the owner; REPAIR_MINIMUM_REMAINING_BUDGET_MS in src/orgunits/classify/repair.ts is 120000 and this file freezes it.

repairContract.minimumRemainingBudgetMsBasis: The owner selected 120000 ms on the usable repair window (2026-09-14). At exactly the floor a worst-case 60000 ms auth-status check still leaves 60000 ms of runner window, with the 10000 ms hard-kill grace already reserved outside the usable window; 60000 exceeds the slowest observed attempt-1 full evaluation (50179 ms) by 9821 ms. The earlier 60000 ms value was rejected because at that floor a worst-case auth-status check consumed the whole window (TIMEOUT, zero inference). minimumRemainingBudgetMsOptions below records both options and their exact residual-time semantics.
rules: disabled behaviour is byte-compatible with the pre-R1 fail-closed path: no repair is planned, no second provider call is made, no repair row or artifact is written, and every attempt-1 artifact is file-for-file unchanged
exactly one repair round per logical evaluation
at most one isolated repair request per initially rejected document; a document is never repaired twice; a repair is never repaired
a repair is triggered only for an item-level EVIDENCE or LENGTH rejection, and only after the original raw output and validation result have been durably persisted

a repair is never triggered by a whole-call SCHEMA_INVALID, a DOC_INDEX rejection, a TIMEOUT, a provider transient exhaustion, an auth failure, a usage-limit outcome, a refusal, any comparison with gold, or an existing repair
each repair request contains only the frozen system prompt and schema, the frozen batch context, the single rejected document, the emitted invalid fields and machine-readable validation reason codes

no sibling document, sibling output, full prior output, gold label, expected answer or programmatic value correction enters a repair request; no unit_name, quote or source is ever corrected, substituted or rewritten by code
repairs are validated by the unchanged validator (src/orgunits/classify/validate.ts) against the single-document batch

repair artifacts are persisted write-once under their derived repair identity (repair-1/doc-<k>/ under the attempt directory; repair call rows linked by repair_of_call_id and repair_doc_index in production)
a failed or timed-out repair leaves the document rejected and never rewrites the original completion or any original artifact

a repair-round TIMEOUT is recorded as the repair’s outcome and the round continues to the next document; it is not by itself an experiment stop; a usage-limit outcome during a repair IS a stop (USAGE_LIMIT_INTERRUPTION)
first-pass validity and post-repair validity are reported separately, always
repairContract.skipRecord: REPAIR_SKIPPED_INSUFFICIENT_BUDGET is persisted, with zero provider calls, when the usable window (remaining minus the hard-kill grace) is below minimumRemainingBudgetMs

callCeiling.rule: Mechanically derived from the frozen batch structure: one original provider request per logical evaluation plus at most one repair request for each of that batch’s documents (the maximum number of initially rejected, item-level-eligible documents is the document count). Each provider request may internally make at most 1 + MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES adapter attempts (class A), so the adapter-attempt ceiling is (1 + documentCount) x (1 + 2). No other bound is claimed; the budget below is the binding limit in practice.

observedNeedOnAttempt1.note: attempt-1 evidence only, not a bound

tier1.operatorReattempt: an operator-authorised reattempt increments attemptNo; it is never an adapter retry

tier2.where: src/test/harness/processIsolatedBatch.ts (test harness only; never a production fallback)
tier2.role: evidence and containment, not production isolation
tier2.watchdogRationale: The auth-status runner (AUTH_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS) can consume up to 60 s before the provider window opens; the provider window (CLASSIFIER_CALL_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS) is 600 s; the last attempt may add up to the 10 s inner close grace (CLASSIFIER_CALL_HARD_KILL_GRACE_MS); 30 s remain for child startup, artifact flushing and scheduling variance. A Tier-2 kill therefore cannot pre-empt a correctly firing Tier 1.

decisionRule.tier1FiresFirstOnOriginal: If Tier 1 returns TIMEOUT before Tier 2 fires: record the evidence (progress trace, stderr tail) and stop; continuation is an operator-authorised attemptNo + 1.
decisionRule.tier1FiresOnRepair: Record the repair outcome as FAILED / TIMEOUT, leave the document rejected, continue with the next document and the next evaluation; not a stop.
decisionRule.tier2KillsBecauseTier1DidNotFire: If Tier 2 kills the batch process because Tier 1 did not fire: process-isolated production inference becomes mandatory follow-up 2D2B-2b, and the experiment stops.

sharedBudgetRule.statement: The original request, its transient backoff sleeps, every repair request’s own pre-flight and auth-status work, and every repair request’s attempts and backoff all consume ONE injectable-clock window of totalProviderCallBudgetMs, opened in the orchestrator or child immediately before the original provider call is entered. A repair’s window is (remaining - abortCloseSettlementGraceMs); the adapter opens a caller-supplied window at classify() entry and never widens it beyond the frozen total; each attempt inside is bounded by min(attemptSoftDeadlineMs, remaining).

perEvaluationWorstCaseMs.proof: Every repair is opened only while usableMs = remaining - grace >= minimumRemainingBudgetMs; its WINDOW (the bound on all of its attempts, backoff and its own pre-flight and auth-status check) is usableMs; each ATTEMPT inside it is bounded by min(300000, window remaining), so no repair attempt ever receives more than the frozen soft deadline. Sequential repairs each re-measure remaining, so the sum of all windows never exceeds the original 600000 ms; at most one hard-kill grace can be outstanding at the end. The child reads the clock before the original classify(), so the original call’s own pre-flight and auth-status time is inside the measured window (conservative). Artifact writes between calls (the original outcome records, each repair’s decision and request records, each repair’s post-call records) are inside the measured window for the NEXT repair; only the round summary and CHILD_RESULT, written after the last repair, fall outside it and inside the Tier-2 variance reserve.

tier2Sufficiency.claim: SUFFICIENT for every provider-facing millisecond: the derivation reserves 60000 ms for the ORIGINAL call’s auth-status runner, 600000 ms for the provider window and 10000 ms for one final inner close grace; under the shared-budget rule the original call, every repair and every repair’s own auth-status check together total at most 600000 ms plus one grace, so this part is proved by the formula, not assumed. The 30000 ms variance reserve must absorb child startup, scheduling, and the write-once repair artifacts written after the last repair (the round summary and CHILD_RESULT) plus any write not already inside the measured window; that residual is a BOUNDED READINESS RISK, not a proved fact: a request-free synthetic persistence benchmark (src/test/unit/orgunitClassify2D2CF0CPersistenceBenchmark.test.ts) writes the maximum per-evaluation repair artifact set with the real fsync-backed writer and must finish inside the reserve on the run machine. No Tier-2 value changes.
tier2Sufficiency.boundedReadinessRisk: Persistence latency cannot be proved by plan-only verification. The synthetic benchmark measures the maximum per-evaluation repair artifact set (1 round summary + 6 x 5 document artifacts = 31 write-once, fsync-backed files at attempt-1-like sizes) on the run machine without any provider or SDK call; the measured value is recorded in the F0C audit. If it approaches the reserve, the watchdog derivation is revisited BEFORE authorisation, never during a run.

sharedBudgetRule.repairTimeoutContinuation: A Tier-1 TIMEOUT of a REPAIR request is recorded on that repair (FAILED / TIMEOUT), the document stays rejected, the original PARTIAL stands, and the experiment continues; the F0B decision rule tier1FiresFirst applies to the ORIGINAL request only. TIER2_WATCHDOG_FIRED_BEFORE_TIER1_TIMEOUT is unchanged and remains a stop.

stopConditions.policy: On any stop condition: persist the available diagnostic record atomically (write-once), then stop the ENTIRE experiment. Never continue into a later batch and never start prompt v2. Resumption requires a separate operator authorisation.

conditions.meaning: Tier-2 grace-phase verdict: the child exited without a shutdown acknowledgement. An unconfirmed harness termination, never a clean batch end.
Tier-2 hard-kill disposition: the tree kill was suppressed because the direct child had already exited. An unconfirmed harness termination.
The parent watchdog expired while no Tier-1 TIMEOUT had been observed. Triggers the 2D2B-2b decision.
The provider returned rawOutput but its canonical serialization and SHA-256 were not durably written before layer-2 validation ran.
A per-batch artifact is absent, unparsable or fails its own recorded hash.
Any recomputed corpus, manifest, prompt, freeze-config or lockfile hash differs from this freeze.
The provider-reported model id is not the requested model id.
Any tool, MCP, browser, settings-source, session-persistence or environment-leak violation observed in any attempt.

A USAGE_LIMIT_EXHAUSTED outcome. Stops the experiment; a later separately authorised continuation is idempotent by input identity and never counts against quality (protocol section 8 treatment retained).
Any non-OK provider outcome, or a thrown failure, that cannot be reconciled to exactly one recorded batch attempt with a persisted diagnostic record.
